start.content: I was there. Not at the edge of the crowd, but near Him. I had leaned against His chest at the Last Supper and heard His heartbeat. Now I watched Him lift His hands — those same hands that had touched the leper, that had broken the bread, that had been nailed to the cross and then shown to Thomas. He blessed us. And then He began to rise.

cloud.content: It was not a storm cloud. It was the glory cloud — the same one that led Israel through the wilderness, the same one that filled the Temple at its dedication. It swallowed Him whole, and when it parted, He was gone. But the glory remained.

feeling.content: Grief had been my companion for weeks. But in that moment, it was replaced by something else. A fullness. He had said, 'I am with you always.' And as He rose, I understood — He was not leaving us orphaned. He was sending the Helper.

understanding.content: I had written His signs down from the beginning. The water turned to wine. The man born after given sight. Lazarus called from the tomb. Each sign pointed to this day. The Son of Man did not come to stay, but to ascend. To open the way. To sit at the right hand of the Father and intercede for us.

angels.content: Two men in white robes. Their faces were grave, not with condemnation, but with urgency. 'Why do you stand looking into heaven?' they asked. As if we should have known better. As if we should have been moving, not staring. The promise of His return settled in my chest like an anchor. He would come back. The same way. The same body. The same power.

closing.content: I went back to Jerusalem and wrote. Not just what I had seen, but what it meant. The Word became flesh. The Word ascended. And the Word will return. Everything I witnessed points to that.
